From Wiktionary, the free dictionary
See also: веревка

Russian

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old East Slavic вьрвь (vĭrvĭ) + -ка (-ka), from Proto-Slavic *vьrvь (deverbal of *verti), from Proto-Indo-European *wer- (“to tie, string; rope”) which is ultimately cognate with *wer- (“to turn, bend”) whence the two meanings of the verb. Compare Belarusian вяроўка (vjarówka), Ukrainian верве́чка (vervéčka), Old Church Slavonic връвь (vrŭvĭ). Non-Slavic cognates include Lithuanian virvė, Latvian virve, Latgalian vērve (“rope, cord, line”), Ancient Greek ἐρύω (erúō, “I drag, pull”) and Sanskrit वरत्रा (varatrā).

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [vʲɪˈrʲɵfkə]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)

Noun

[edit]

верёвка • (verjóvka) f inan (genitive верёвки, nominative plural верёвки, genitive plural верёвок, relational adjective верёвочный, diminutive верёвочка)

  1. rope, line
    Synonym: бечёвка (bečóvka)
